TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Banda Sea, 2034
DATE 14 March 2034 · 0120 local
SIDE USA
WINDOW 80 min, closes at 120
YF-23 prototype. Photo: U.S. Air Force · Public domain · cropped

BANDA SEA, MARCH 2034. A mobile launcher complex threatens the north-eastern passage. An RQ-180 is ahead of the bomber package; the escort includes YF-23s, two Fury wingmen off Enterprise and aircraft carrying long-range missile fits.

Opposing J-36 and J-50 fighters cover the complex, with a Tu-95MA contributing a further missile threat. Earlier imagery narrows the launcher search area, but mobile equipment must be located and identified before attack.

Strike the launcher complex and preserve a recovery route for the package. Darwin is beyond the escorts' reach on this task: they recover to Langgur in the Kai Islands or to USS Enterprise, south-east of the track.
Air Component, 2034
COMMANDER'S INTENT

The bomber package must neutralise the assigned launcher complex. Use the reconnaissance picture to support the strike, protect the escorts and keep a recovery route open. New equipment does not remove the need to identify targets or conserve fuel.
• Put the stream's release on the launcher complex
• Keep the escort fighters alive
• Keep the RQ-180 alive

Two YF-23, one F-15EX, an F-16CM with JATM, a Rafale F5, two FQ-44 Fury wingmen (escort and EW), the RQ-180, a B-52O, a B-1B and a B-52H in the stream. Opposing: J-36, J-50, a Tu-95MA with Meteorit, a Type 004 picket and a relocatable launcher complex.

The planned window is 80 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 40 minutes more; the operation is closed at 120 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
